content:
Hi folks!

I'm not a mathematician but I've played with Lean a bit. Figured this might be contained enough that someone here can answer. (Mathematical parts of this post are AI-generated; I've tried to verify what I understand.)

I've been trying to vibecode my way towards Conway's refinement conjecture that Oz has the refinement property: when bc = de you can write b = fg, c = hi, d = fh, e = gi. AFAIK that's the same as every element being primal, so everything below is about primality.

I haven't had much luck with the conjecture itself. However, I did end up with a Lean proof of this statement which my AI says doesn't seem to be in the literature:

Every element of K((ℝ^{≤0})) whose support has order type below ω^ω is primal.

I can't tell whether that's interesting or new, so that's what I'm asking.

This is all against L'Innocente–Mantova, A factorisation theory for generalised power series and omnific integers (Adv. Math. 442, 2024), cited below as [LM24]. K has characteristic zero throughout.

Known: order type below ω

[LM24, Cor. 6.3.9] says that every series with finite support is primal in K((ℝ^{≤0})).

In Lean, I have finite support written as ot < ω, where ot is the order type of the support. I figured it's easier to share definitions first in case they're misleading.

Here's my definition (i.e. a Prop) of this statement from LM24:

variable (K) in
/-- [LM24, Cor. 6.3.9]. Mathlib's `IsPrimal` is [LM24, §2.5]'s primal, and `a : nonpos K` makes
the divisibility in `K((ℝ^{≤0}))`, not in the finite-support subring `K(ℝ^{≤0})`. -/
def FiniteSupportIsPrimal [CharZero K] : Prop :=
  ∀ a : nonpos K, ot (a : HahnSeries ℝ K) < ω → IsPrimal a

I'd love a check on whether this statement accurately reflects that part of [LM24, Cor. 6.3.9].

(There's a link further below for the full REPL with statements.)

Maybe new (?): order type below ω^ω

Here's a similar proposition, but instead of ω let's raise it to ω^ω:

variable (K) in
/-- Not in [LM24]. The irreducible ones are then prime [LM24, §2.5]. -/
def FiniteDegreeIsPrimal [CharZero K] : Prop :=
  ∀ a : nonpos K, ot (a : HahnSeries ℝ K) < ω ^ ω → IsPrimal a

This is the possibly new thing.

I couldn't find this statement in the literature.

(Note: ot < ω^ω is the same as deg < ω, for the degree of [LM24, §1.5].)

Statements in Lean

My main question is about the statements themselves.

I put the above statements into this REPL. I deliberately kept them very thin and used Mathlib only so they should be easy to digest. If these are misstated or trivial, I would very much appreciate knowing that!

These are definitions only, but I do also have their proofs in a WIP repository. The proofs are on top of my own formalization of a chunk of [LM24] plus a formalization of my AI-generated "paper". #print axioms returns only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. If this is interesting to anyone, I'll clean it up and publish the repository.

Relation to Conway

Conway's conjecture is that Oz is pre-Schreier. By [LM24, Thm. 9.0.1], that can only hold if rings of the form K((ℝ^{≤0})) are pre-Schreier too.

[LM24, Cor. 6.4.2] says these three are equivalent:

  1. K((ℝ^{≤0})) is pre-Schreier.
  2. It's a GCD domain.
  3. Every irreducible series with infinite support is prime.

The new statement doesn't close any of these, but it gives (3) for order type below ω^ω, since an irreducible series that is primal is prime. It doesn't say anything for higher order types.

Existing results

Here's what my AI was able to find in existing literature:

  • Degree 0. [LM24, Cor. 6.3.9], the finite-support one above.

  • Degree 1. Pitteloud proves primality for order type ω and ω + 1, for series with v₀ = ω (Existence of prime elements in rings of generalized power series, JSL 66 (2001) 1206–1216, §3). [LM24, Thm. F] covers order type ω +̂ k. [LM24, Cor. 7.2.12] goes further inside degree 1, under extra hypotheses.

  • Degree 2 and up. I couldn't find anything. If it exists, I'd appreciate pointers.

The new statement reaches degree 2. For example, exponents -(1/2)^m - (1/2)^(m+1+n) for m, n : ℕ give a support of order type ω^2, and I have a Lean proof that element is primal.

What I want to know

  • Are the definitions above misstated?
  • Is it worth writing up properly, or is the "new" statement boring / obvious?
  • Is this already known, or does it follow from something known that I missed?

Happy to answer questions, although I'll have to direct the mathematical ones to AI since I'm doing more of a "non-technical PM" role here.

Thanks!

Note: unrelated but maybe useful. The second example in [LM24, §1.5] doesn't work as printed. ∑_{(m,n)} t^{-1/(n+1)(m+1)} is said to have order type ω^2. But (n+1)(m+1) runs over every positive integer, so the support is {-1/k : k ≥ 1} and the order type is ω. The same slip is in Remark 2.7.2. There the first summand of ∑_{(n,m)} t^{-1-1/((n+1)(m+1))} + ∑_n t^{-1/(n+1)} has order type ω, not ω^2, so the stated degree is 1 rather than 2. Exponents like -1-1/(n+1)-1/((n+1)(n+m+3)) do give ω^2.

I don't know the math, so can't answer any of the questions, but a passing remark:

Your "here is file with all the definitions and theorems with sorries, can humans spot check it" sounds very similar to the comparator setup people are doing with many autoformalized repos (e.g. https://github.com/rkirov/list-color-function/blob/main/comparator/Challenge.lean). Might be good idea to do setup that for your repo too. It is quickly becoming the "golden standard" of autoformalization.
